idiom_name: Foundation Notification + NotificationCenter (name, object, userInfo); Codable enum for the wire contract
implementation_notes: Foundation ships the pattern: Notification is a ready-made event message (a Notification.Name type tag, an optional source object and a userInfo payload), and NotificationCenter is the channel - post(name:object:userInfo:) broadcasts to any registered observer, addObserver(forName:object:queue:using:) subscribes with a queue, notifications(named:object:) exposes the same stream as an AsyncSequence, and publisher(for:) bridges it to Combine. Nothing must be subclassed: the occurrence is described by posting, the receiver by observing. For typed payloads and cross-process delivery the idiom is a Codable enum (or struct) serialised with JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder; NotificationCenter itself is in-process only, so a broker client or DistributedNotificationCenter (macOS IPC) carries events beyond the process.
pitfalls: userInfo is [AnyHashable: Any] - untyped and not serialisable; wrap the payload in a Codable message type when it must cross a process or be validated.
Closure-based observers must be removed via the returned token, and the posting thread delivers unless a queue/actor is given; AsyncSequence iteration needs a cancellation boundary.
Notifications are broadcast to every observer of that name, so a duplicate post (e.g. from a retry) is a duplicate event: consumers must be idempotent.
Posting synchronously from a critical section runs observers inside it; hop to a queue or actor when observers do real work.
